original_question: For each complexity class C among VWaring, VChow, and VBP, determine whether the class equals its corresponding border analogue.
target_in_paper: Section 3.1, Problem 15: the debordering question for the homogeneous classes VWaring, VChow, and VBP.
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the exact open problem stated in the paper: after defining the homogeneous classes VWaring, VChow, and VBP and their border counterparts, the paper asks whether each class equals its corresponding border analogue. It also correctly keeps the scope to these three classes, rather than drifting to the weaker neighboring Problem 16.
missing_details: The paper works over the complex numbers C and explicitly restricts this discussion to the homogeneous setting.

The objects in the classes are p-families (f_n)_{n in N} of homogeneous polynomials f_n in S^{d_n} C^{N_n}, where both the degree d_n and the number of variables N_n are polynomially bounded functions of n.
VWaring and VChow are defined using polynomially bounded Waring rank R_V(f_n) and Chow rank R_Ch(f_n), not just informal circuit classes.
R_V is the rank with respect to the Veronese variety, and R_Ch is the rank with respect to the Chow variety Ch_{N,d} of products of d linear forms.

VBP is defined using polynomially bounded iterated matrix multiplication complexity imm_C(f_n), equivalently ABP width in the homogeneous setting; imm_C(f) is the least r such that f can be written as M_1 ... M_d with matrix sizes 1xr, rxr, ..., rx1 and linear-form entries.

The border analogues are obtained by replacing R_V, R_Ch, and imm_C with their semicontinuous border versions; the paper explicitly defines border imm_C(f) as the minimum r for which f is a limit of polynomials f_epsilon with imm_C(f_epsilon) <= r.
The quantifier is over each of the three classes individually: the question is whether each class, viewed as a set of p-families, is equal to its own border class.
No nilpotency condition or 'for all sufficiently large m' clause appears here; the relevant growth condition is polynomial boundedness in the family parameter n.
refined_question: Working over C in the homogeneous setting, let (f_n)_{n in N} be a p-family with f_n in S^{d_n} C^{N_n}, where d_n and N_n are polynomially bounded in n. Let VWaring, VChow, and VBP be the classes of such p-families for which, respectively, the Waring rank R_V(f_n) (rank with respect to the Veronese variety), the Chow rank R_Ch(f_n) (rank with respect to the Chow variety Ch_{N,d} of products of d linear forms), and the iterated matrix multiplication complexity imm_C(f_n) are polynomially bounded in n, where imm_C(f) is the least r such that f = M_1 ... M_d with M_1 in C^N tensor Mat_{1xr}, M_j in C^N tensor Mat_{rxr} for 2 <= j <= d-1, and M_d in C^N tensor Mat_{rx1}. Define the corresponding border classes by replacing each measure with its border/semi-continuous analogue, in particular border imm_C(f) = min{r : f = lim_{epsilon -> 0} f_epsilon with imm_C(f_epsilon) <= r}. For each C in {VWaring, VChow, VBP}, is C equal to its corresponding border class?
justification: This is Problem 15 in Section 3.1, stated immediately after the paper introduces the homogeneous p-family framework, defines VWaring, VChow, and VBP, and then defines their border analogues. The earlier notation paragraph fixes the ambient field as C, and equation (1) with the adjoining paragraph provides the general rank and border-rank notions that underlie Waring rank and Chow rank. Nearby Problem 16 is related but weaker and different, asking whether VWaring is contained in border-VChow and, more modestly, for upper bounds on Waring rank in terms of border Chow rank, so it should not replace your draft.
